Integer partitions

Source: R/combinatorics-partitions.R
IntegerPartition.Rd

IntegerPartition(partition, integer) stores a partition of an integer, as SymPy's IntegerPartition. The partition is a vector of positive integers or a named vector of multiplicities (names are the parts); when integer is given first, as in SymPy, the parts must add up to it. The fields $partition, $integer and $conjugate mirror SymPy's. next_lex() and prev_lex() step through the partitions of the integer in lexical order, as_dict() gives the multiplicities and as_ferrers() draws the Ferrers diagram. Comparisons follow SymPy's (< and <= compare the parts from smallest to largest).

Usage

IntegerPartition(partition, integer = NULL)

as_dict(p)

as_ferrers(p, char = "#")

prev_lex(p)

next_lex(p)

random_integer_partition(n, seed = NULL)

Arguments

partition

Parts, or the integer when integer gives the parts.

integer

The parts, or NULL.

p

An IntegerPartition.

char

The character for the Ferrers diagram.

n

A positive integer.

seed

A seed for SymPy's _randint.

Value

An IntegerPartition; as_dict() a named integer vector, as_ferrers() a string and random_integer_partition() an integer vector.

Details

random_integer_partition(n, seed) draws a random partition; seed follows SymPy's _randint (an integer seed or a vector of values to use).

Examples

a <- IntegerPartition(c(5, 4, 3, 1, 1))
a
#> [5, 4, 3, 1, 1]
a$conjugate
#> [1] 5 3 3 2 1
next_lex(IntegerPartition(c(3, 1)))
#> [4]
as_dict(a)
#> 5 4 3 1 
#> 1 1 1 2 
cat(as_ferrers(IntegerPartition(c(1, 2, 3))))
#> ###
#> ##
#> #
random_integer_partition(10, seed = c(1, 3, 2, 1, 5, 1))
#> [1] 5 2 1 1 1
